chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Dawud ibn Mihran, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi, from a man, from Juwayriyya ibn Mus'har, who said:

I hurried behind the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O Juwayriyya! Those fools were not destroyed except by the slapping of their shoes behind them.' He asked: 'What brought you?' I said: 'I came to ask you about three things: about nobility, and about chivalry, and about intellect.' He said: 'As for nobility, then whoever is ennobled by the Sultan is noble. And as for chivalry, it is the rectification of one's livelihood. And as for intellect, whoever fears Allah is intellectual.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of intellect (aql) and nobility (sharaf) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Juwayriyya ibn Mus'har seeks clarification on three key virtues from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who redefines nobility not as lineage but as political recognition, chivalry as the practical management of one's livelihood, and intellect as the spiritual state of God-consciousness (taqwa). This definition highlights the Shia emphasis on internal piety as the true measure of wisdom, distinguishing it from worldly status.
